title: Key stream give-up on the turn lease instead of a fixed window
description:
**Follow-on to `6bd49c`, raised 2026-09-17. Do NOT start this before `65b431`.**

`6bd49c` gave the turn stream a fixed 10-minute inactivity window before it gives up. A fixed window is the wrong mechanism once legitimate silence can be long: any number picked is either too short for real work or too long to detect a dead worker.

The system already has an authoritative liveness signal. A working worker renews its lease (`renew_turn_lease`, `control_plane.py:3178`), and a parked turn carries `waiting_for`. The watchdog decides exactly this way (`handle_turn_deadline`, `control_plane.py:3232`): waiting means healthy, lease valid means healthy, otherwise recover.

## What to do

Replace the fixed window with the same test. On the idle backoff cadence — not every poll — re-read the turn record and give up only when it is still `ACTIVE`, `waiting_for` is None, and `lease_expires_at` has lapsed past a grace margin.

Gains:
- Work of any duration streams for as long as the worker keeps renewing. No ceiling to tune.
- A genuinely dead worker is detected in roughly lease time (60-120s) instead of 10 minutes.
- One definition of "alive", shared with the watchdog, so the two cannot drift apart. The 10-minute constant disappears.

## Why the ordering is strict

Today the lease lapses during legitimate tool work, because the worker does not renew while a tool runs (`65b431`). Keying the stream on the lease before fixing that would make the stream give up on healthy turns — worse than the fixed window it replaces.

## Already partly done

The `waiting_for` half shipped separately as a defect fix: the 10-minute window did not check for parked turns, so a turn waiting on a human longer than 10 minutes drew a spurious `turn.reconciling` while the control plane considered it healthy. `_turn_is_parked` in `http/app.py` now guards that. This card is the remaining half — the lease check that lets the fixed window be deleted.

## Done when

`stream_turn` has no fixed inactivity constant, gives up only on a lapsed lease for a turn that is neither parked nor terminal, and a test covers a long-running turn that keeps renewing and is never closed.
